maria: Hey — I'm seeing a socket/file-descriptor leak when cancelling async streaming responses in the Python SDK. Seems tied to the auth refresh path firing while an SSE/chunked stream is active.

maria: Minimal repro (async):
```py
async with Client(token=short_lived_token) as c:
    async for chunk in c.stream('/v1/generate', json=payload):
        if should_cancel(chunk):
            break  # expect this to close underlying connection
```
If the token expires and the client triggers a refresh during the stream, after breaking out the socket stays in TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED and descriptors pile up.

sam: can you share python/aiohttp versions and whether you're using the SDK's refresh or custom handler?

maria: python 3.11.7, aiohttp 3.9.4, built-in auth refresh. Steps: run a loop that opens a stream, cancel after first chunk, rotate server token to force 401 on next request, let refresh run. After ~50 iterations netstat shows many sockets not reclaimed until process restart.

kevin: do you see any "coroutine was never awaited" or similar runtime warnings? my guess is finalizer/weakref path isn't awaiting .release()/.close(). That leaves the transport open.

maria: yes — "RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'ClientResponse.release' was never awaited" appears intermittently. Also occasionally see "RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine" when opening subsequent streams.

natalie: current public typing exposes stream() as AsyncIterator[bytes], but impl returns an async generator with a weakref finalizer. That's error-prone. We should offer an AsyncContextManager (async with) so __aexit__ can await cleanup. Also update typing to make resource semantics explicit.

sam: temporary workaround: wrap in try/finally and await the internal close helper:
```py
try:
    async for chunk in c.stream(...):
        break
finally:
    await c._transport_close()  # internal hack to force response.close()
```
Not ideal but stops FD growth for me.

kevin: proposal: change stream() to return an object that implements AsyncContextManager and yields an AsyncIterator. Example API:
```py
async with client.stream(...) as gen:
    async for chunk in gen:
        ...
```
Then __aexit__ can await response.close(). Also ensure auth refresh spawns an awaitable tied to the request lifecycle (cancelable) instead of a detached background task.

maria: strong +1. I'll draft repro + logs into an issue. Can also attach netstat diffs and traceback.

natalie: typing suggestion: class Stream(AsyncIterator[bytes], AsyncContextManager[AsyncIterator[bytes]]): ... and implement aclose()/__aexit__ semantics. Add mypy tests that fail if people try to ignore the context manager.

sam: add a tiny example in examples/ showing proper cancel semantics. Many users just break the async for and assume the SDK closes things. We should make safe usage obvious.

kevin: i'll work on a minimal, non-breaking shim: keep stream() convenience but return a proxy that logs warnings if garbage-collected without being closed, and have __iter__ raise advising to use async with. Then a major version can flip semantics. Also add integration tests that simulate 401 mid-stream.

maria: CI note: I reproduced this inside a container and used strace to see close() not being called on the socket. Also captured runtime warnings. I'll paste the small reproducer in the issue.

ci-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/2298 - "async stream: token refresh during stream can leak socket / not await response.close()" :white_check_mark:

kevin: assigning self for the API change, will open PR with tests and a compatibility shim.

natalie: i'll take typing/tests and add tox env for aiohttp matrix (3.8/3.9/4.x). Add mypy- strict-check job so this kind of resource misuse gets caught.

sam: thanks. maria pls drop your reproducer script into the issue so we can run in CI. Also note exact aiohttp/pypy/uvloop combos if you tried alternatives.

maria: will do. TL;DR until patch lands: either use explicit async with pattern if available or call response.release()/await c._transport_close() in finally. I'll update the issue with reproducer and logs. :thumbsup:
